paraphrased_content: Section 3(k) lists computer programmes per se and algorithms among excluded subject matter.
review_note: Preliminary record; Section 3(k) concerns algorithms/software and is excluded from Ayurvedic formulation classification index

paraphrased_content: Section 3(p) excludes from patentability an invention which in effect is traditional knowledge or which is an aggregation or duplication of known properties of traditionally known component or components.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds patent traditional knowledge exclusion; submitted for Harshit activation review

document_title: Food Safety and Standards Ayurveda Aahara Regulations 2022
paraphrased_content: Regulation 2(b) defines Ayurveda Aahara as food prepared according to authoritative books listed in Schedule A, excluding Ayurvedic drugs, proprietary medicines, cosmetics, and parenteral administration; Regulation 3(4) strictly prohibits adding vitamins, minerals or amino acids.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-15; narrowed to statutory text of reg. 3(4) (vitamins, minerals, amino acids ban) and reg. 2(b) exclusions

document_title: Food Safety and Standards Ayurveda Aahara Regulations 2022
paraphrased_content: Regulation 8 strictly prohibits labelling or advertising claiming prevention treatment mitigation or cure of human disease; Regulation 13(a) mandates front-of-pack display of the official Ayurveda Aahara logo on the principal display panel.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-15; locators corrected for disease claims prohibition (reg 8) and front-of-pack logo (reg 13a)

paraphrased_content: The rules were notified on 22 October 2024 with commencement on 21 December 2024 (sixty days post-Gazette notification per NBA FAQ); prescribes procedures and Form 7/Form 8 for access to biological resources and IPR applications.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-15; notification 22 Oct 2024 and commencement 21 Dec 2024 per NBA FAQ; Form 7/8 updated

paraphrased_content: Biological Diversity Amendment Rules 2025 were notified on 6 May 2025 and commence on 1 November 2025 per NBA FAQ; update administrative filing procedures, timelines, and fee schedules for commercial utilization and IPR filings.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-15; notification 6 May 2025 and commencement 1 Nov 2025 per NBA FAQ

paraphrased_content: WIPO GRATK Treaty establishes a mandatory patent disclosure requirement: applicants must disclose country of origin or indigenous source for inventions based on genetic resources or associated TK.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; international overview context only; does not create direct domestic law

paraphrased_content: TKDL provides access to its structured prior-art database to designated international patent offices under bilateral non-disclosure access agreements to prevent wrongful patent grants.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; defensive protection framework verified; confidential records excluded

paraphrased_content: Ayurvedic Siddha or Unani drug includes medicines for diagnosis treatment mitigation or prevention of disease in humans or animals manufactured exclusively in accordance with formulae described in First Schedule authoritative books.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds Route 1 Classical ASU; submitted for Harshit activation review

paraphrased_content: Patent or proprietary medicine in relation to ASU systems means a formulation containing only ingredients mentioned in First Schedule authoritative books but not included in authoritative formulae; excludes parenteral administration.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds Route 2 Patent or Proprietary ASU; submitted for Harshit activation review

paraphrased_content: Cosmetic means any article intended to be rubbed poured sprinkled or sprayed on or introduced into or applied to the human body for cleansing beautifying promoting attractiveness or altering appearance.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds Route 6 Ayurvedic Cosmetic; submitted for Harshit activation review

paraphrased_content: Phytopharmaceutical drug means purified and standardized fraction with defined minimum four bioactive or phytochemical compounds of an extract of a medicinal plant or its part non-parenteral regulated under CDSCO framework.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14 (GSR 918(E) 2015); grounds Route 4 Phytopharmaceutical referral; submitted for Harshit activation review

paraphrased_content: A substance obtained by a mere admixture resulting only in the aggregation of the properties of the components thereof or a process for producing such substance is not an invention.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds ASU patent admixture exclusion; submitted for Harshit activation review

paraphrased_content: The mere discovery of a new form of a known substance which does not result in the enhancement of the known efficacy of that substance or mere discovery of any new property or new use is not an invention.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14 (Act 15 of 2005); grounds ASU patent efficacy requirement; submitted for Harshit activation review

paraphrased_content: Section 6(1) as amended by Act 10 of 2023 (effective 1 April 2024) mandates that persons referred to in Section 3(2) (foreign individuals, non-residents, or entities with foreign participation) must obtain prior approval of the National Biodiversity Authority (Form 7) before grant of an intellectual property right in or outside India.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-15; amended s. 6(1) foreign applicant approval before grant via Form 7 (effective 2024-04-01)

paraphrased_content: Under Section 6(1A) as amended by Act 10 of 2023 (effective 1 April 2024), persons referred to in Section 7 (domestic Indian entities and citizens) must register with the NBA (Form 8) before grant of an intellectual property right, and under Section 6(1B) obtain approval before commercialization. Section 6(2) governs benefit sharing determination. The proviso to Section 7(1) exempts local vaids and hakims from commercial intimation but does not waive patent registration or approval requirements under Section 6.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-15; corrected subsections to s. 6(1A) domestic registration, s. 6(1B) commercialization approval, and proviso to s. 7(1) for vaid/hakim exemption

paraphrased_content: For classical Ayurvedic medicines the licensing applicant must cite the recognized First Schedule book name and submit the exact classical formula without modification; missing book citation requires clarification and cannot be demoted to proprietary.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-15; grounds evidentiary requirements for Classical ASU license and safe clarification fallback

paraphrased_content: For patent or proprietary ASU medicines the licensing applicant must furnish published scientific literature safety data and proof of effectiveness before license grant.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds safety and literature requirements for P&P ASU

document_title: Guidelines for Examination of Patent Applications on Traditional Knowledge 2012
paraphrased_content: Patent examiners must assess whether claimed herbal combinations represent mere aggregations of known traditional properties under Section 3(p); requires applicant to prove unexpected synergy with comparative data.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds administrative examination standard for Section 3(p) and 3(e)

document_title: Guidelines for Examination of Patent Applications on Traditional Knowledge 2012
paraphrased_content: In assessing traditional knowledge patent applications examiners must conduct mandatory prior-art searches in TKDL and classical literature before granting any claims.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds TKDL examination procedure

paraphrased_content: FSSAI order clarifies that Ayurveda Aahara products must strictly display the official logo obtain dedicated FSSAI licensing and refrain from advertising disease-cure benefits under penalty of law.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds operational enforcement compliance for food products

paraphrased_content: Phytopharmaceutical new drug applications require formal CDSCO submission of animal pharmacology acute/chronic toxicology formulation standardization and human clinical trials.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds strict regulatory burden distinguishing phytopharmaceuticals from ASU

paraphrased_content: The First Schedule to the Drugs and Cosmetics Act lists 54 authoritative treatises of Ayurveda (e.g. Charaka Samhita Sushruta Samhita AFI API) governing classical formulae.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds statutory definition of recognized classical texts

document_title: Food Safety and Standards Ayurveda Aahara Regulations 2022
paraphrased_content: Schedule A of the Ayurveda Aahara Regulations lists the authoritative Ayurvedic books recognized for recipes and ingredients used in food preparations.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds food recipe compliance for Ayurveda Aahara

paraphrased_content: WIPO GRATK Treaty Article 6 provides for the establishment of information systems and databases of genetic resources and traditional knowledge in consultation with indigenous peoples and local communities.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-15; locator corrected to Article 6 (Article 5 covers sanctions and remedies)

paraphrased_content: Patent specifications must disclose the source and geographical origin of the biological material in the specification when used in an invention.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds mandatory biological origin disclosure for patent applications

paraphrased_content: The patent applicant must submit a declaration in Form 1 regarding biological material obtained from India and declare whether NBA approval has been sought or obtained.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds patent procedural declaration on biological resources

paraphrased_content: Statements of commercial working of patented inventions in India must be submitted periodically under Form 27 as amended by Patents Amendment Rules 2024.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds commercial working verification requirements

paraphrased_content: Rule 170 of Drugs Rules 1945 (previously requiring prior approval for ASU drug advertisements) was omitted by the Central Government via Gazette notification G.S.R. 360(E) dated 1 July 2024; active advertising prohibitions are governed by the Drugs and Magic Remedies Act 1954.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-15; omitted by G.S.R. 360(E) dated 1 July 2024; documented as historical supersession to prevent false active guidance

paraphrased_content: Prohibits the advertisement of certain drugs for treatment of specified diseases and disorders listed in the Schedule including cancer diabetes blindness and kidney disorders.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds statutory prohibition against miraculous or schedule disease advertisements

paraphrased_content: No person shall take part in the publication of any advertisement relating to a drug if the advertisement contains any matter which directly or indirectly gives a false impression regarding the true character of the drug.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds false impression and consumer deception prohibitions

paraphrased_content: The National Biodiversity Authority determines benefit sharing obligations which range from 0.1 percent to 0.5 percent of annual ex-factory gross sales for commercial utilization of biological resources.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds economic ABS benefit sharing percentage formulas

paraphrased_content: Claims made for food products shall not be false misleading or deceptive and shall not refer to suitability for prevention alleviation treatment or cure of a disease disorder or particular physiological condition.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds general food advertising and non-medicinal claims standards

paraphrased_content: Applicants seeking approval for phytopharmaceutical drugs must submit comprehensive scientific data on botanical taxonomic authentication chromatographic fingerprinting and multi-marker standardization.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds scientific chemical profiling standards for phytopharmaceuticals

paraphrased_content: Farmers shall be deemed to be entitled to save use sow resow exchange share or sell their farm produce including seed of a variety protected under this Act; delineates plant variety protection from patent monopolies.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-14; grounds farmers rights and boundary with biological patent exclusions

paraphrased_content: WIPO GRATK Treaty Article 5 establishes sanctions and remedies prohibiting the revocation of patent rights solely on the basis of failure to disclose genetic resources or TK unless there was fraudulent intent.
review_note: Verified by Thulasi 2026-11-15 against official WIPO text; grounds patent remedy limits and non-revocation protections
